lessons: Tukey IQR fences are unusable as an outlier rule on thin samples and were shipped that way. At n=4 and n=5 the outlier lands inside the half it is measured against and inflates it, so the fence outruns the row it should catch: [10000,10100,10200,10300,100000] gives Q3=55150 and an upper fence of 122,800, flagging nothing. Enumerated n=4..12: only n>=4 was guarded, but n=4 and n=5 both fail in BOTH directions. Replaced with the Iglewicz-Hoaglin modified z-score against the median (MAD), which is robust at n=4, survives 2 contaminated rows of 5, and false-flags clean data slightly LESS often (13.0% vs 15.1%).

The low-side miss is the dangerous one in this domain and was not what the reporter emphasised. A gift or partial-share row recorded far BELOW market drags the median down and makes a property look cheap, which is exactly the direction someone contesting a bank appraisal would misuse. Always test an outlier rule in both directions, not just the eye-catching high one.

A guard threshold is not the same as a working method. The code said 'if len(deals) < 4: do not flag', which reads as a considered floor, but at n=4 and n=5 the method silently flagged nothing while the output still advertised a median that excluded outliers. A statistical guard must be validated at the boundary it claims to protect, not just assumed. Enumerate every n from the floor upward.

When porting a script rule into prose for the manual path, the prose inherits the bug. Step 2b had told agents to hand-apply the IQR fences, so the same blind spot existed on the no-shell route and had to be fixed in both languages too.

v1.1.0 shipped a WRONG claim that the nadlan MCP 'returns aggregates, not deal rows, so it cannot feed Steps 3 to 7'. It is false: get_valuation_comparables returns individual deal rows with gushNum/parcelNum and accepts area/room/floor/radius/deal_type filters. Root cause: an expert subagent asserted it and I encoded the assertion without reading the MCP's own tool list or API reference. Same failure mode as the original bug being fixed (a confident unverified mechanism), one layer up. Verify a subagent's factual assertions about a THIRD-PARTY artifact against that artifact before writing them into the skill.

A local MCP process is the automation path on Claude Desktop specifically, because it runs on the user's machine and therefore uses their network rather than the assistant's. It does NOT help on claude.ai/ChatGPT/Manus, where nothing runs locally. Do not describe 'MCP' as a uniform bypass across no-shell hosts.

The user's own agent reported 'the network here is restricted to technical domains only', i.e. a CLIENT-SIDE egress allowlist, which is a different mechanism from the geo/datacentre block named in the skill. The skill's hedged wording survives this, but if a third data point points at an allowlist, promote that to the primary explanation.

get_valuation_comparables does not filter to residential natures and lets non-residential rows into its own market_statistics (verified: a מלאכה row became the min and p25 of price-per-sqm for הרצל 10 חיפה). Never quote a third-party tool's aggregate block without checking what rows it aggregated.

Root cause of the 2026-08-02 user report was NOT a rotated Govmap token. Live probe from an Israeli egress returned 200 on all four chain endpoints with the embedded apiKey. The skill's own Troubleshooting row asserted 'the public token was rotated', and the agent relayed that wording to the user verbatim as a confident diagnosis. A troubleshooting table that guesses a cause will be quoted to users as fact: only list causes that have been verified, and label the unverified part as unverified.

The skill declared claude-desktop, claude-ai, chatgpt and manus in supported_agents while its only data path was a Python script. Whenever supported_agents includes a no-code-execution host, every step that shells out needs a stated alternative route, or the skill is broken on that host by construction. Re-check this invariant on any future step that adds a script.

A fallback path that replaces a script must restate the script's ARITHMETIC, not just its filters. The first draft of Step 2b listed nature/band/window/outlier filtering but omitted the price-per-sqm basis, median-not-mean, the IQR threshold and the four-row floor, which left the manual path materially looser than the script it replaced. When porting a script's behaviour into prose, walk the script top to bottom and port every decision rule, including the ones that only fire on small samples.

Do not describe an MCP as a network-level bypass without checking where it runs. The first draft claimed the nadlan MCP 'works where a direct call does not' for all four no-shell clients; that only holds for a locally-running process. A remotely hosted MCP sits on the same refused ranges. Also verify an MCP can return the SHAPE of data the step needs. [CORRECTED in v1.1.1: the claim originally recorded here, that nadlan returns aggregates and can never feed a comparables analysis, was WRONG. get_valuation_comparables returns deal rows. Do not carry that claim forward.]

Link-check note: gov.il landing pages lazy-load their main content, so a Playwright snapshot taken immediately after navigate shows an empty <main> and reads as a dead page. Wait a few seconds and re-check the page title before flagging a gov.il URL as broken. nevo.co.il and gov.il both 403 under curl and render fine in a browser; neither is a broken link.
